evidence_snippets: On Compute Engine or GKE, you must authenticate with the cloud-platform scope . // Import the Secret Manager client library. use Google\Cloud\SecretManager\V1\Client\SecretManagerServiceClient; use Google\Cloud\SecretManager\V1\AddSecretVersionRequest; use Google\Cloud\SecretManager\V1\SecretPayload; / @param string $projectId Your Google Cloud Project ID (e.g. 'my-project') @param string $secretId Your secret ID (e.g. 'my-secret') / function add secret version(string $projectId, string $secretId): void { // Create the Secret Manager client. $client = new SecretManagerServiceClient(); // Build the resource name of the parent secret and the payload. $parent = $client->secretName($projectId, $secretId); $secretPayload = new SecretPayload([ 'data' => 'my super secret data', ]); // Build the request. $request = AddSecretVersionRequest::build($parent, $secretPayload); // Access the secret version. $response = $client->addSecretVersion($request); // Print the new secret version name. printf('Added secret version: %s', $response->getName()); } Python To run this code, first set up a Python development environment and install the Secret Manager Python SDK .
